title: Logical operators
recap: Logical NOT ! inverts a boolean value, logical AND && is true only when both operands are true, and logical OR || is true when either operand is true. Parentheses make mixed logical requirements easier to verify.

The && and || operators short-circuit from left to right: they do not evaluate the right operand when the left operand already determines the result. Keep side effects out of conditions unless that sequencing is deliberate and clear.
objectives: Combine required and alternative access conditions with && and ||.
Use ! to reject a suspended account.
Group mixed logical operators to communicate the policy.
Test the policy with several deterministic scenarios.
warnings: Bitwise &, |, and ~ are not substitutes for logical &&, ||, and !.
Do not depend on precedence when parentheses make a mixed condition clearer.
Avoid mutating state inside a condition merely to exploit short-circuiting.
challenge: Implement canEnter(). Entry requires a badge, requires either staff status or an appointment, and rejects suspended people. Print results for an appointed visitor, a staff member without a badge, and a suspended staff member.
hints: The badge requirement belongs on the left side of &&.
Group isStaff || hasAppointment because either one satisfies the role requirement.
Complete the expression with && !isSuspended, then print booleans with std::boolalpha.

contains: bool canEnter(bool hasBadge, bool isStaff, bool hasAppointment, bool isSuspended)
